name: Elhanan
overview: Elhanan is a male figure mentioned in the Old Testament as the son of Jaare-oregim. He is notably identified as the seventh member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's warriors, highlighting his role as a distinguished soldier during King David's reign. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Elhanan means "G-d [El] is gracious," reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with Hebrew naming traditions. This proper name emphasizes God's gracious character but is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elhanan as the son of Jaare-oregim. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elhanan's significance in the biblical narrative rests primarily on his inclusion among "the thirty," a select group of David's mighty men, underscoring his valor and importance in David's military exploits. His identification as Jaare-oregim's son provides a genealogical anchor, though the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds. His mention contributes to the broader understanding of David's leadership and the men who supported him.
